description: A solo developer passionate about technology, space exploration, and innovation. I work on identifying the locations of Earth, Moon, and Mars using agentic AI approaches. With experience in vibe coding, web development, game development, and AI agent building, I aim to turn creative ideas into practical solutions.
summary:
ASTRA (Autonomous Scientific Terrain Research & Analysis) is an AI-assisted platform for identifying potential Earth analog locations for Moon and Mars missions. Site selection is complex because terrain, geology, temperature, resources, and hazards must be evaluated together. ASTRA brings these factors into one evidence-led workflow
Users select a lunar or Martian target region, define mission priorities, and compare it with potential Earth analog sites. The platform combines Earth and planetary data, including elevation products, surface imagery, and environmental measurements. Geospatial tools derive comparable features, while a transparent scoring method ranks candidates using configurable mission-specific weights.
ASTRA goes beyond a single score. It displays feature-level comparisons, data coverage, uncertainty, mismatches, and dataset sources, helping users understand results and identify evidence gaps. An AI research agent helps explore findings, answer questions using retrieved evidence, and create explanations and reports. Scientific measurements and similarity scores are calculated deterministically; the AI does not invent data or rankings.
Built with Python FastAPI, a web interface, geospatial tools, and a database, ASTRA makes planetary site research more accessible. Earth analogs are partial comparisons, not exact replicas of lunar or Martian conditions. ASTRA helps researchers identify promising locations, understand trade-offs, and guide scientific validation.
details:
ASTRA – Autonomous Scientific Terrain Research & Analysis is an AI-assisted planetary analog discovery platform designed to help researchers identify potential Earth locations that resemble selected lunar and Martian regions. It addresses the challenge of comparing complex scientific factors such as terrain, geology, temperature, resources, and surface hazards during planetary mission planning.

How it works: Users select a Moon or Mars target region and define mission priorities. ASTRA evaluates potential Earth analog locations using available scientific and geospatial datasets. It extracts comparable features, calculates transparent similarity scores using configurable weights, and ranks candidate locations. Users can explore results through an interactive map, scientific comparisons, feature-level evidence, data coverage, uncertainty, and source information. An AI research agent assists users in exploring findings and understanding the results.

Benefits and intended impact: ASTRA brings multiple scientific parameters into one platform, making planetary analog research more accessible, structured, and evidence-driven. It can help researchers and mission planners shortlist promising locations for field studies, simulations, and further validation. It aims to support better-informed research and contribute to future Moon and Mars exploration.

Tools and technologies: The project uses Python and FastAPI for the backend, HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the frontend, SQLite and SQLAlchemy for data management, and geospatial libraries such as NumPy, Pandas, GeoPandas, Rasterio, and Shapely. Leaflet.js supports interactive mapping, while Chart.js and ReportLab support data visualization and report generation. The platform uses scientific datasets and services from sources such as NASA.

Creativity and design considerations: ASTRA combines deterministic scientific calculations with an AI-powered research assistant. Unlike a basic chatbot or map, it focuses on explainable comparisons rather than unexplained rankings. The design considers data availability, measurement compatibility, scientific accuracy, uncertainty, mission-specific priorities, and the limitations of Earth-based analogs. It does not claim that Earth locations perfectly reproduce lunar gravity, vacuum, radiation, or the Martian atmosphere.

Team: Team Jerry – Solo project.
